# cortex-ia — Full Context

cortex-ia detects supported coding-agent targets, compiles canonical Go workflow IR, renders target-specific assets, diagnoses compatibility, and installs one immutable plan with backup, receipt, post-doctor, and receipt-backed rollback.

## Authority

- ForgeSpec owns versioned SDD contracts and authoritative task readiness/claim/status.
- Cortex owns durable evidence, provenance, memory, and relationships.
- Runtime-native dispatch owns child execution transport only.
- cortex-ia owns compilation, configuration, diagnosis, installation, backup, receipts, and restoration.

## Execution profiles

`portable-sequential` requires no delegation. `portable-flat` requires fresh direct-child evidence. `native-advanced` uses only independently qualified capabilities. ForgeSpec `direct-v1` requires every P0 capability; ForgeSpec 1.2.x may run only as `legacy-sequential`. Missing optional P1 file reservations forces disclosed sequential/no-concurrent-write execution.

The orchestrator dispatches one ForgeSpec-ready bounded reference directly to `implement`. The historical `team-lead` role is retired and absent from every current profile.

## Retired compatibility and external data

The historical Agent Mailbox identifier remains only for bounded legacy decode, exact owned-registration migration, rollback, and operator cleanup guidance. Provider-neutral remote A2A is unsupported and unbound. External Mailbox database, WAL/SHM files, caches, archives, and repository checkout are never automatically mutated or deleted; cleanup is operator-controlled after preservation checks.

Counts for components, services, tools, adapters, profiles, and goldens are derived from source inventories and negotiated schemas rather than caller-declared documentation values.
